column1: # Format:  term<TAB>weight     (see terms.en.tsv for what the weights mean)
# ── WHY THIS TIER EXISTS, AND WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE ARABIC ONE ───────
# Hostnames are ASCII. An Arabic-audience adult site is almost never registered
# in Arabic script — it is `sks-arab.com`, not `سكس-عرب.com`. So an
# Arabic-script-only term list matches essentially NO hostnames, and the whole
# network-layer keyword mechanism (the layer that closes the threat model's
# "new domain, registered today" row, system-wide, for every app on the Mac)
# would be a no-op for exactly the audience this product is built for.
# This tier is also what catches Franco-Arabic written in page text, which is
# how a large share of Arabic-speaking users type online.
# Franco-Arabic substitutes digits for letters that have no Latin equivalent:
# `terms.normalize()` does NOT fold these away — they are letters here, not
# decoration — so write them exactly as people type them. `token_variants()`
# strips only a TRAILING digit run, which is hostname decoration ("sks123"),
# never a leading or embedded one ("3ahira").
# Spelling is not standardised, so the same word appears several ways. List
# every common variant rather than hoping normalisation will bridge them — it
